title: Knowledge check: Vue Application Security

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Vue Application Security”?
options: Render untrusted values as escaped text, validate input and URLs, and enforce access decisions on the backend.
Compile untrusted strings as Vue templates to make them interactive.
Use a hidden frontend button as the only authorization check.
Treat a VITE_ environment variable as secret because it came from .env.
questions.answer_key: Render untrusted values as escaped text, validate input and URLs, and enforce access decisions on the backend.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Vue Application Security directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Rendering untrusted content safely”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Compile untrusted strings as Vue templates to make them interactive.
Use a hidden frontend button as the only authorization check.
Treat a VITE_ environment variable as secret because it came from .env.
Render untrusted values as escaped text, validate input and URLs, and enforce access decisions on the backend.
questions.answer_key: Render untrusted values as escaped text, validate input and URLs, and enforce access decisions on the backend.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Rendering untrusted content safely”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Vue Application Security” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
